problem: Prior VLN tasks such as R2R give a single, fully specified and unambiguous route instruction. Prior interactive navigation work (VLNA, HANNA) gives help as templated or generated language, and Talk the Walk uses an abstract map with a known target. No dataset had two-sided, free-form human-human dialog in which an ambiguous, underspecified goal hint must be resolved through questions and answers while both speakers share an egocentric photorealistic view.
motivation: Robots in homes should be able to ask for help in language and understand the human replies. That requires data in which navigation is interleaved with natural question and answer exchanges. The observation driving the paper is that real dialogs show egocentric references, conversational repair, and references back to earlier dialog and navigation. An agent therefore likely needs the whole dialog history, not just the latest instruction, and human navigator demonstrations are noisy but informative about long-range exploration.
key_idea: Collect 2050 human-human Navigator/Oracle dialogs in Matterport3D, where the Oracle sees the next 5 shortest-path hops. Turn them into the Navigation-from-Dialog-History (NDH) task: given a target-object hint plus the Q/A history, move toward the goal room, scored by goal progress in meters.
insight: (1) Mixed supervision beats both pure human and pure planner supervision, statistically significantly across all folds (with one exception) under paired t-tests with Benjamini-Yekutieli correction. It uses the human Navigator path when it passes through the end of the Oracle's shortest-path segment, and the Oracle path otherwise, which acts as a binary confidence filter on human demonstrations. Test-unseen goal progress for the full-history model is 2.35 m mixed vs 2.11 m navigator vs 1.25 m oracle. (2) Only the full dialog history gives a statistically significant gain over the target-object-only model in unseen test houses: 2.35 vs 1.90 m. Seen houses are dominated by visual memorization: the vision-only unimodal model reaches 5.72 m vs 5.92 m for the full model. (3) Naively concatenating an LSTM encoding of the navigation history did not help (val-unseen mixed 2.10 → 1.84 m), suggesting cross-modal attention is needed. A large gap to the human-like Shortest Path upper bound remains (about 8-10 m).
method: CVDN data collection: paired AMT workers. The Navigator moves through the Matterport3D nav graph and can ask questions or guess the goal room; the Oracle sees a mirrored view plus an animation of the next 5 shortest-path hops and answers in free text. The hint is 'The goal room contains a t_o', where t_o is one of 81 object types occurring 2-4 times per house, so the hint is ambiguous and underspecified. The start node is chosen to maximize distance to all candidate goal regions.

NDH task construction: each dialog <N0,Q1,A1,N1,...,Qk,Ak,Nk> yields one instance per exchange i. Input is t_o plus the history (Q_1:i, A_1:i); the agent starts at the end of N_{i-1}. This gives 7415 instances: 4742 train / 382 val-seen / 907 val-unseen / 1384 test-unseen, following R2R scan folds.
Goal Progress (GP) metric: reduction in topological distance (m) to the closest node of goal region G_j, measured between the agent's start and end nodes.

Seq2Seq agent (R2R baseline style): an LSTM encoder over learned token embeddings of the dialog history, with NAV/ORA/TAR/EOS tags, utterances kept in order but reversed at the token level, and max length up to 720 tokens. It initializes an LSTM decoder that takes ImageNet ResNet-152 features of the current egocentric frame and outputs low-level actions.

Supervision variants: Oracle path O_i (≤5 hops), Navigator path N_i (human, up to 40 hops), and Mixed M_i = N_i if e(O_i)∈N_i else O_i. Training uses student-forcing with cross-entropy against the next shortest-path action to the supervision end node, for 20k iterations at batch size 100. Max episode length is 20 for oracle and 60 for navigator/mixed.

Ablations/baselines: a Shortest Path agent as an upper bound (with navigator supervision it approximates human performance), a Random agent, unimodal baselines (vision-only, language-only, neither), and dialog-history truncations (t_o only, +A_i, +Q_i, full history). The appendix adds a navigation-history (N_H) concatenation variant.

setting.backbone: LSTM seq2seq encoder-decoder (trained from scratch) with frozen ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-152 visual features
setting.training_data: CVDN/NDH train fold (4742 instances from 2050 dialogs, 83 Matterport houses); for the test-fold evaluation, trained on train+val folds. No extra/synthetic data.
setting.observation: egocentric single-view RGB frame (ResNet-152 features) + dialog history text + target object token
setting.action_space: low-level R2R simulator actions: turn left/right, tilt up/down, forward to adjacent nav-graph node, stop
setting.privileged: none at test time (the Oracle's shortest-path view is only used during data collection and training supervision)

numbers_note: Only Goal Progress (m) is reported; there is no SR/SPL. Validation numbers are the best across all evaluated epochs (optimistic model selection); test uses the epoch best on val-unseen. The best val-seen number is the mixed t_o+A_i+Q_i variant at 6.16, not the full-history model. The appendix Table 4 adds a +navigation-history variant (val-seen 5.82, val-unseen 1.84 mixed), which is not listed here.
results: The full-dialog-history Seq2Seq agent with mixed supervision reaches 2.35 m goal progress on test-unseen (2.10 m val-unseen, 5.92 m val-seen). On test-unseen it beats Random (0.83), vision-only (1.74), language-only (1.40) and the target-object-only model (1.90), and it is the only history setting that is significantly better than target-only on test. Mixed supervision significantly outperforms navigator-only (2.11) and oracle-only (1.25) supervision. The human-like Shortest Path upper bound (8.48-9.76 m) shows large headroom.
limitations: Discrete graph-based Matterport3D navigation with RGB only; transfer to real robots (depth, noise, localization, continuous motion) is not addressed.
The baseline is a simple Seq2Seq that ignores navigation history (naive concatenation hurt) and has no cross-modal attention; results are far below human-level goal progress.
Only the navigation half of the dialog is studied; question asking/answering agents and end-to-end two-agent evaluation are left to future work.
